advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In the live guard test, assert that the review-bot scan visited modules and found the known publishes (`review_bot_artifact_emit_errors` exact, `review_bot_llm_` prefix) before trusting the empty overlap.
evidence: tests/unit/test_review_bot_single_metric_publisher.py:148-149: `assert not unresolved, ...` / `assert not offenders, (` (absence-only; no presence assertion from the same scan)
tests/_tree_scan.py:39: `for path in sorted(root.rglob("*.py")):` (an empty or missing root gives an empty tuple and no error)
Only the probe side has a liveness anchor (lines 97-102). Nothing asserts that the scan saw `review_bot_artifact_emit_errors` (artifact_emit.py:37) or the `review_bot_llm_` prefix (voter.py:133).
advisory.finding: test_review_bot_never_publishes_a_metric_the_host_probe_publishes is a fail-open oracle on the review-bot side. It asserts only `not unresolved` and `not offenders` and never checks that the module scan ran or found the metrics review-bot is known to publish. If `_REVIEW_BOT` stops pointing at the package (move or rename), `parsed_python_files` returns an empty tuple, because `rglob` on a missing directory yields nothing, and the guard passes. The same happens if `_calls_put_metric_data` stops matching.
scenarios: The review_bot package moves (e.g. src/rebar/review_bot -> src/rebar/services/review_bot). The guard scans zero modules and stays green while a reintroduced voter_errors publish double-counts again.
The put_metric_data call moves into a shared helper outside review_bot, or is called via getattr. Every module returns empty sets and the guard passes without checking anything.
advisory.suggested_fix: Collect `all_exact` and `all_prefixes` across modules in the loop. Before the absence asserts, add `assert parsed_python_files(_REVIEW_BOT)`, `assert "review_bot_artifact_emit_errors" in all_exact` and `assert "review_bot_llm_" in all_prefixes`, so a blind scan fails rather than passing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the scanner also read `MetricName=` keywords in `dict(...)` calls (or report them as unresolved), and add a synthetic test of a module with both a literal dict and a `dict(MetricName='voter_errors')` publish.
evidence: tests/unit/test_review_bot_single_metric_publisher.py:47: `if isinstance(node, ast.Dict):` (keyword-form `dict(MetricName=...)` is an ast.Call, never inspected)
tests/unit/test_review_bot_single_metric_publisher.py:75-76: `if not values:` / `unresolved.append(... "no MetricName literal was found")` (only fires when NO dict literal exists in the module)
tests/unit/test_review_bot_single_metric_publisher.py:66-68 docstring: `Anything else ... is reported as unresolvable, so an empty overlap can never come from a name the scan could not read.`
src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:133: `"MetricName": f"review_bot_llm_{field}",` (an existing literal in the module where voter_errors used to be published)
advisory.finding: The scanner misses a MetricName passed as a keyword to `dict(...)` whenever the same module also has any dict-literal MetricName. `_metric_name_values` collects only `ast.Dict` keys, and `unresolved` is filled only when that collection is empty. Concrete bypass: add `boto3.client('cloudwatch').put_metric_data(Namespace='rebar/host', MetricData=[dict(MetricName='voter_errors', Value=1, Unit='Count')])` to voter.py, which already has the literal `"MetricName": f"review_bot_llm_{field}"`. The guard then reports no overlap and nothing unresolved, so the exact double count from this bug comes back undetected. No synthetic test covers a mixed module like this.
scenarios: A future change restores a best-effort voter_errors publish in voter.py using `dict(MetricName="voter_errors", ...)`. The guard passes, and two timeouts page again.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_metric_name_values`, also walk `ast.Call` nodes whose func is `Name(id='dict')` and add the value of any `keyword(arg='MetricName')`. Add a test that parses a module with `{'MetricName': f'review_bot_llm_{x}'}` plus `client.put_metric_data(MetricData=[dict(MetricName='voter_errors', Value=1)])` and asserts that `overlaps(...) == {'voter_errors'}`.
